project_summary.objective: The core objective of this research is to identify and address upcoming major global concerns—spanning environmental, social, and geopolitical issues—by combining several A.I. models leveraging their individual analytical strengths and analyzing historical relationships between interrelated crises. This analysis will hopefully lead to the development of a comprehensive algorithm designed to assist future decision-makers in preventing, mitigating, and managing global concerns more effectively.

historical_analysis.description: The research examines past interrelated crises (e.g., economic downturns coinciding with natural disasters) to determine how these events compounded or mitigated one another.
historical_analysis.goal: Gain insights into patterns of crisis escalation or resolution to refine future response strategies.

algorithm_development.description: The data from historical crises is used to build an algorithm that predicts how emerging global concerns may interact, either compounding or mitigating each other.
algorithm_development.purpose: To offer decision-makers a dynamic real-time assessment tool.

testing_and_teaching.testing: Once developed, the algorithm will be tested against historical scenarios to validate its predictive accuracy and applicability to modern crises.
testing_and_teaching.teaching: The algorithm will form the foundations for a proposed Global Crisis Management Organization (GCMO) roleplay where students are taught to apply its insights through realistic crisis management simulations.

project_summary.impact: This research aims to enhance crisis response and decision-making by equipping future leaders with practical tools. The algorithm offers a proactive means to address looming global concerns, ensuring decision-makers can rely on data-driven strategies. The GCMO will help pass this knowledge to the next generation of leaders, preparing them to handle complexities in an interconnected and fragile world.
